## assistant - 2026-08-29T04:00:48

Session is running continuously. Status at 00:00, 9 h to the 09:00 deadline:

**Tonight's headline result — repeatability, which is what the manuscript needed.** Across 8 independently screened areas, **12 of 13 lattice panels drove the director to their own commensurate member, median offset 1.5°**. And the film moves *exactly as far as it is sent*: distance-moved falls on the 1:1 line against distance-to-travel from 10° to 75°.

**A new quantitative result that strengthens the mechanism.** The commensurate lattice rewrites at **σ 144** (12.7× null) where an aperiodic square needs 400–667. So matching the wavevector **cuts the required dose by at least 3×** — selection isn't a passive direction-chooser added onto drive, it lowers the barrier. Every dose from 144 to 803 cleared, and above threshold the response is *not graded* (w scatters 0.40–0.95 over a 2.6× dose range, tracking area not dose), which is what a barrier crossing looks like.

**Two failures worth noting, both handled correctly.** One queue job aborted on the C21 per-site charge limit — at Λ 354 nm a panel holds only 64 sites, so σ 667 needs 20.4 V·s/site. The gate was right; σ is now capped by the charge limit rather than losing the area, and "coarse film cannot be written as hard as fine film" is a real recipe constraint. And I reconciled 71 unbilled write-minutes into the S24 ledger — the drivers now charge the cap and refuse writes it can't cover.

**Written so far:** FINDINGS M20 (grade A), `MANUSCRIPT_DRAFT.md` with every claim flagged **[SOLID]** or **[NEEDS]**, and `make_manuscript_figures.py` regenerating all figures and statistics from the CSV so prose and data can't drift.

Running now: ring-2 area probe, then round 2 of the queue — dose 20–110 to find where the lattice finally *fails* (currently a bound, not a measurement), plus selection repeats 6–7, a third lattice-vs-aperiodic, and a third shear test. 36.5 write-minutes remain, queue costs 23.8.

**A claim I had to withdraw, and it's the most useful thing that happened tonight.** The 23-point dose series showed the two lowest doses (σ 19, 28) missing target by 56–64° while everything ≥52 landed within 6° — a textbook threshold, and it would have been the campaign's sharpest number: selection switching on ~10× below the aperiodic square.

Both failures came from **one area with Λ 388 nm**, the coarsest in the set. At that Λ the 1.4 µm analysis window holds **3.6 periods — under the estimator's 4Λ minimum**. Two panels agreeing because they *share a defect*, not because they share physics. And the trap is structural: the low-dose end of a series is exactly where the estimator is also weakest, so a real threshold and an estimator failure appear at the same place by construction.

Recorded as **PITFALLS 19.15**, and the driver now refuses any area whose readout window holds fewer than 4Λ (Λ ≤ 350 nm at this window size) and flags 4.0–4.3Λ as marginal. Note the campaign already screened Λ for *buildability* (M9) — but never checked the *readout* window was valid at that Λ. Two different requirements that happen to involve the same quantity.

**What survives is still strong:** on valid film the lattice is on target at every dose from **σ 52** upward — 4–6° at 52–117, tightening to 1.0–1.5° above 144. That's ≥8× below the aperiodic square's 400–667. But it's a *bound*, not a measurement.

Round 3 is therefore aimed squarely at that gap: eight low-dose runs (σ 20–110) on fine film with repeats, costing ~3 write-minutes of the ~9 remaining — the expensive high-dose repeats are already banked. Ring-3 area probe is running now to supply the fine areas.

## assistant - 2026-08-29T05:32:32

**This is the most interesting result of the night.** In both genuine misses, the failed panel landed on its **neighbour's** commanded director — within 14° and 3.5°:

```
(0,8)    P1 want  14.0 -> 10.0  HIT        P2 want 134.0 -> 0.0   (14.0 deg from P1's target)
(16,16)  P1 want  16.5 -> 10.0  HIT        P2 want 136.5 -> 20.0  ( 3.5 deg from P1's target)
```

Both times P2 abandoned its own template and adopted P1's director. The two panels are 2.0 µm apart, centre to centre — a 0.6 µm gap. That suggests **lateral crosstalk**: a written orientation propagating into a neighbouring panel and overriding its template.

Consistent with this, every miss occurred in a `select` run (the only design where the two panels have *different* targets); all the dose and shear runs, where both panels share a target, had zero misses — crosstalk would be invisible there by construction.

The honest caveat: with 3 triad members, a random miss lands near the neighbour's target ~1/3 of the time, so two-for-two is p ≈ 0.11 by chance. Suggestive, not proven. Recording it and building the discriminating test:

Round 3 is set and waiting on the ring-3 probe. The queue now costs **7.2 write-minutes of the 9.5 remaining** — affordable because dwell scales with dose, so a `select` run at σ 120 costs 1.1 min instead of 5.5.

It answers the two open questions:

**(A) Crosstalk — 6 runs, matched design.** Same dose, same targets, *only the gap changes*: three at the 0.6 µm gap that produced the defections, three at 1.8 µm. If a written domain really does propagate into its neighbour, the wide arm shouldn't defect. If the misses were random, the rate won't move. This is worth the budget because it's the only hypothesis that explains any failure, and because it would set a **minimum pitch for independently addressable features** — directly relevant to whether this is a usable patterning technique.

**(B) Threshold — 2 runs, σ 20–60 on fine film**, replacing the two points I had to discard for the 3.6Λ window problem.

Statistical honesty up front: three runs per arm is thin. At the observed 40% defection rate I'd expect ~1.2 defections in the narrow arm, so a clean zero in the wide arm would be suggestive, not conclusive. I'll report it that way rather than overclaiming from n=3.

Current state: **30 panel rows**, 22/24 on target on valid film (median offset 1.5°), FINDINGS through M21, PITFALLS through 19.15, manuscript draft and figure pipeline both regenerating from the CSV.

That's now PITFALLS 19.15, and the driver refuses windows under 4Λ.

What survives is still strong and defensible: on valid film the lattice is on target from **σ 52** upward, ≥8× below the aperiodic square — stated as a bound, not a measurement.

### 19.15 The dose threshold that was really a window-size limit

Twenty-three dose points, sigma 19 to 803, on a commensurate lattice. Two of
them missed their target badly -- 64 and 56 degrees off -- and they were the two
lowest doses. Read naively that is a threshold: selection switches on somewhere
between sigma 28 and 52, ten times below the aperiodic square's 400-667. It

======================================================================
### M13 — The tip writes: 180 deg out-of-plane reversal under +10 V, demonstrated · **A**

- **Why it was asked.** Three in-plane iterations on 28 Aug came back VOID. One
  was explained by a collapsed readout (M12) and one was not: its after-frames
  were the *stablest* part of the iteration (after-vs-after floor 0.145, 0 %
  flips) and the panels still moved no more than the untouched tiles did
  (excess 0.008 and 0.017). Before spending more time on dose, the question
  "does any bias reach the sample at all" had to be settled.
- **Operation:** `diag_poling.py`. Two solid 1.2 um squares written side by side
  at **+10 V and -10 V**, raster pitch 60 nm, 0.25 um/s, areal dose
  ~667 V.s/um^2 (~1.7x the lattice that failed), per-site 2.0 V.s. VDART before
  and after. Both polarities, because the film reads 88-96 % one class: whatever
  the starting state, one square must be writing against it.
